chunks: As for what Saʿd narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yāsīn al-Ḍarīr, from Ḥarīz ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, that he was asked about a surah with which a man prays in the two rakʿahs of the obligatory prayer.
He said: Yes; if it is six verses, he may recite half of it in the first rakʿah and the other half in the second rakʿah.
So this report is to be understood as applying to the state of taqiyyah, not to the state of choice; that is indicated by what follows.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation/precautionary conformity in conditions requiring it
key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: the two rakʿahs of the prayer
key_terms.الْخَبَرُ: the report or hadith under discussion
key_terms.حَالِ الِاخْتِيَارِ: the state of normal choice and non-compulsion
key_terms.سِتَّ آيَاتٍ: six verses in the surah being discussed

ai.seo_question: Can half of a surah be recited in each rakʿah of an obligatory prayer?
ai.summary: This report discusses the recitation of a surah across the two rakʿahs of an obligatory prayer. The final statement clarifies that this ruling is carried on taqiyyah rather than the normal rule of choice, indicating a juristic qualification in how the hadith is applied.
